arbiter.summary: Two distinct, real defects in herd/briefs/tsofficeagent.md, each reported twice under different framings. (A) Lines 397-400: git fetch and git merge-base --is-ancestor are unchained statements with no set -e/&& gating the latter on the former's success; on a fetch failure the ancestry test silently compares stale cached refs (refs/tmp/Nhead and origin/main persist across runs in the shared worktree ref store) and can print HEAD CONTAINS MAIN against an untested remote head, which the downstream gate (qodo-cycle/pre-merge-checks-gate.sh:134-168) cannot catch because it reads only check-run state, never sha/ancestry. Findings 0 and 3 are the same code site and same mechanism (0 is framed as a report, 3 as the fix instruction) -- one code change (require fetch success before the ancestry test) closes both. Fails toward silence, so agreed severity is medium, matching the skeptic's correction on both. (B) Lines 240-276: the dispatcher's three-condition inertness test is satisfied by a live, resumable agent merely awaiting an async response or an armed wake signal -- backlog-loop/SKILL.md's own resumption design guarantees exactly this shape. The brief explicitly permits leaving such an agent running while spawning a replacement on the same ticket, and backlog-loop/SKILL.md:813-821 documents this exact pattern having already caused an unaudited merge. Findings 1 and 2 are the same race (1 generic, 2 review-notification variant); both confirmed high, both fix_now. No refutations were supplied, so unsound_refutations is empty by default, not by omission of scrutiny.

confirmed.title: Failed fetch still reports stale cached refs as current
confirmed.summary: Failed fetch still reports stale cached refs as current
confirmed.failure_scenario: First run the check successfully with origin/main=A and refs/tmp/Nhead=H, where H contains A. A sibling then advances remote main to B, which H does not contain. On the next run, make fetch fail through an authentication or network failure. Because the ancestry command is not conditional on fetch succeeding, it compares the cached A and H, prints HEAD CONTAINS MAIN, and exits successfully. The existing green CI checks can then authorize a merge that never tested B. This disproves the added claim that fetching both refspecs prevents the stale-base false positive.

No `set -e`, and a grep of the whole 482-line brief finds no instruction to require fetch success. Linked worktrees share the common ref store, so refs/tmp/Nhead and refs/remotes/origin/main persist from a prior successful run; on an auth/network fetch failure the ancestry test compares the cached A and H, prints HEAD CONTAINS MAIN and exits 0 — exactly the silent-direction fail-open the added paragraph (:402-409) claims the second refspec removes. Nothing downstream catches it: qodo-cycle/pre-merge-checks-gate.sh:134-168 reads only check-run `state`, never a sha or ancestry. Extra aggravation: the ref name is the PR-independent literal refs/tmp/Nhead, so a failed fetch can answer the ancestry question using another PR's cached head. Medium rather than high only because the failing fetch still writes to stderr (-q suppresses progress, not errors), giving an attentive operator a signal the recipe itself does not require them to check.

confirmed.title: Two quiet ticks do not revoke a live agent's ability to resume
confirmed.summary: Two quiet ticks do not revoke a live agent's ability to resume
confirmed.failure_scenario: An inherited implementation agent has read a file and is awaiting a delayed model/API response across two consecutive 20-minute dispatcher ticks. Its tool subprocess has exited, its host runs outside the worktree, and it produces no commits, pushes, messages, or filesystem changes during that interval. All three inertness conditions pass although the agent remains live. The new rule explicitly permits leaving it running while starting its replacement. When the delayed response arrives, both agents can resume the same claimed ticket and mutate its shared PR; a continuation reusing the original tree can also have its edits overwritten by the original agent's pending write. Observing inactivity supplies no cancellation or ownership handoff, contradicting the assertion that leaving the agent running costs nothing.

confirmed.reasoning: herd/briefs/tsofficeagent.md:243-245 defines inertness purely as (0 processes with cwd in the worktree, no new commits/pushes, no output), and :247-248 permits leaving such an agent running while spawning — 'leaving it costs nothing'. The repo's own backlog-loop/SKILL.md:159-164 establishes the contradicting mechanism: 'a fire notifies EVERY time it stops with no live background children, and it resumes when an armed wake signal (a review poll, an audit) reports' — so a resumable agent has by construction no live children and no output, and an audit/poll host need not have cwd in the fire's worktree. All three conditions therefore pass for a live, resumable agent across two 20-minute ticks; the test observes no cancellation or ownership handoff. Impact is documented as already realised in backlog-loop/SKILL.md:813-821: a 'completed' fire resumed on its wake signals, two fires pushed to one branch, the pre-merge audit ran on an earlier head and the merged code was never audited. The new rule relaxes the ListAgents skip-guard that was the only enforcement of that gate (SKILL.md:164: 'ListAgents is the only reliable check'), and :274 extends the same insufficient test to spawning a continuation on the SAME ticket. High: it re-opens the audit-bypass race the loop exists to prevent.

confirmed.title: Inactivity does not prevent an ignored agent from resuming
confirmed.summary: Inactivity does not prevent an ignored agent from resuming
confirmed.failure_scenario: Fire A awaits an asynchronous review notification for more than 20 minutes, with no shell process, filesystem changes, or messages during two consecutive ticks. The new test permits the dispatcher to ignore A without stopping it and spawn continuation B on the same ticket. When the notification arrives, A resumes while B is editing the same branch; either can overwrite the other's changes or push after the other's audit. backlog-loop/SKILL.md documents this exact resumption mechanism and a resulting unaudited merge. This disproves the claim that leaving the ignored agent running 'costs nothing': observed inactivity provides no exclusion against future writes.

confirmed.title: Abort the freshness check when fetching fails
confirmed.summary: Abort the freshness check when fetching fails
confirmed.failure_scenario: A previous successful check leaves refs/tmp/Nhead=H and origin/main=M0, with M0 an ancestor of H. A sibling then merges M1 into remote main. Run the displayed commands in an ordinary shell while a transient connection failure prevents fetch from updating either ref. Because the ancestry command is not conditional on fetch succeeding, it compares the cached refs, prints HEAD CONTAINS MAIN, and returns success. Once connectivity recovers, the existing CI gate accepts H's green checks against M0, allowing a merge against untested M1. This reproduces the stale-base failure the added instructions claim to prevent; require fetch success before testing ancestry.
